newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end mixed in thin, lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end mixed in thin, lacklustre trade.

text.p: Shares ended mixed in thin, newsless dealings ahead of the weekend.
Blue chips were mired by disinterest while the Second Board were firmer on a rebound, traders and analysts said.

"The market has rebounded but is still lacklustre. There's no excitement, no volume," said Vickers Ballas research manager Irene Tan. The blue-chip focused Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange Composite Index ended in the positive, up 1.82 points to 1,140.74 to reverse four days of losses.
The Second Board index gained 7.61 to 579.79. Total volume was 166 million with 311 gainers and 213 losers.
"The active shares are the second board and lower liners, but even here, the volume is not much," said an institutional dealer.
Second board computer firm MCSB continued to climb on speculation of a takeover and rumoured sofware deal. The stock rose 75 cents to 27.25, off from a new year high of 29.00.
The top gainers table were headed by a clutch of second boarders. They include Bridgecon, Repco, Sunchirin and EMC Logistics which gained between 1.70 and 3.25 ringgit.
Shares linked to Berjaya were active, probably reacting to group asset reshuffling, dealers said.
